title: Preserve focus order and announceable sequence across locale variants and compact layouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Audit and implement design fixes so that keyboard focus order, screenreader announcements, and live-region sequencing remain consistent across localized content (including RTL and CJK) and the console's compact/dense layout variants. This ticket covers design decisions, prototype validation, and front-end acceptance criteria for rollout-related UIs (variant selector, canary toast, rollout inspector) and cost/dashboards tables where column collapse and truncation change DOM order.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard tab order is logically consistent and matches visual order in English, German, Japanese, and Arabic builds for the rollout inspector and cost table variants.

When localized copy expands or contracts, focusable controls do not jump positions unpredictably; focus is preserved or moved predictably with an announced rationale in a screenreader-friendly live region.

ARIA live regions announce rollout state changes (canary start/stop, variant switch) in a single, concise message without repeating previous announcements; announcements do not interrupt typing / editable focus areas.
Compact/dense table mode keeps a predictable focus sequence; collapsing optional columns moves non-interactive content out of the tab sequence rather than reordering interactive elements.

All updated text tokens and interactive controls meet contrast ratio thresholds: 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large UI elements; color tokens for positive/negative badges have accessible fallbacks in both light and dark themes.
Screenreader users can discover the current rollout variant and its active status in under two tab stops from the top of the inspector panel in every supported locale.
Unit tests and E2E keyboard navigation tests added to the console test harness for the primary flows described.
Design prototype validated with at least three assistive-technology testers (NVDA/VoiceOver/JAWS) across two locales and feedback incorporated.
design_notes: Root causes identified in audit: (1) DOM order was being changed during column collapse by moving entire TD nodes which shifted tab order; (2) announcement live regions were duplicated across components causing repeated reads in some locales with longer strings; (3) toast insertion used focusable elements for progress which accidentally trapped focus in localized builds. Proposed fixes: keep interactive DOM order stable and visually hide non-essential content, centralize a single announcement region per page with dedupe/tokenized messages, and make toasts inert unless explicitly actionable (Add 'Open' button only when required).
decisions: We will adopt a 'DOM-stability-first' rule: never relocate interactive controls in DOM order to implement a visual collapse; instead, remove non-interactive content or move it into aria-hidden containers. We will deprecate per-component live regions in favor of a consolidated top-level announcer component that exposes a small set of templated messages to reduce localization variance. Color token adjustments will be limited to existing semantic tokens (info/success/warning/critical) to avoid token sprawl.
next_steps: Ship updated design tokens for contrast fallback (Design -> Tokens PR)
Frontend: implement announcer component and replace component-level live regions (ENG-22134)
Frontend: change table collapse behavior to hide non-interactive cells with aria-hidden instead of reordering (ENG-22165)
Run assistive-technology validation session with 3 testers and log findings in Confluence
Add keyboard nav E2E tests to Cypress harness and mark unstable flows behind feature flag for staged rollout
comments: 2026-02-24 Marcus Patel: Initial audit notes attached — there are two failing keyboard-nav stories in Japanese where long labels push a control off-screen. I've mocked a compact mode where we move the label into a tooltip instead of changing DOM order.

2026-02-28 Sofia Ramirez (PM): Good catch on the announcer duplication. Prioritize a single announcer for rollout state changes — customers using screenreaders reported noisy updates during our last canary.

2026-03-03 Accessibility review (external tester): VoiceOver on macOS read the same blow-by-blow message three times when the canary toggled quickly. Suggest debouncing to 400ms and coalescing similar messages.

2026-03-06 Design review: Updated Figma flows include a compact-label pattern for wide languages and a collapsed-details approach for RTL. Need engineering feasibility review for 'aria-hidden' strategy on table cells.
